disclaimer: This report is an automated engineering quality indication produced by a prototype. A PASS result means only that the listed tools reported no findings above the policy thresholds for the assessed scope. It is NOT a security certification, does NOT establish ISO 26262 / ISO 21434 / ASPICE compliance, and is NOT an Audi IT or release approval. Checks marked NOT EXECUTED or NOT APPLICABLE provide no assurance.

checks.title: API, MCP, vector-store and web security patterns (semgrep, EAF rules)

findings.message: JWT is decoded without verifying its signature
findings.guidance: Verify the signature with the issuer's key and pin the accepted algorithms (algorithms=["RS256"]).

findings.message: TLS certificate verification is disabled for an outbound HTTP call
findings.guidance: Remove verify=False. If an internal CA is used, pass its bundle (verify="/path/ca.pem").

findings.message: MCP tool runs a shell command or evaluates code; its arguments are chosen by an AI model
findings.guidance: Treat every tool argument as untrusted. Remove shell/eval, call a fixed program with an argument list, and validate arguments against an allow-list. If command execution is the tool's purpose, run it in a sandbox and require human approval.

findings.message: Vector index is loaded with pickle deserialisation enabled
findings.guidance: Only load index files you created and whose integrity you verify (checksum/signature); prefer a store that does not rely on pickle. A tampered index file executes code on load.

findings.message: TLS certificate verification is disabled
findings.guidance: Remove rejectUnauthorized false / NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 and trust the internal CA explicitly (ca option or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS).

findings.message: JWT is accepted without verifying its signature
findings.guidance: Use jwt.verify with the issuer's key and an explicit algorithms list that does not contain "none". jwt.decode does not check the signature.

findings.message: Shell command is built from a template string or concatenation
findings.guidance: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and no shell, and validate each argument against an allow-list.

findings.message: CORS allows every origin together with credentials
findings.guidance: List the allowed origins explicitly. A wildcard origin with credentials lets any website call the API as the logged-in user.

findings.message: MCP server HTTP transport listens on all network interfaces
findings.guidance: Bind to 127.0.0.1 for local use. If the server must be reachable over the network, put authentication (OAuth 2.1 per the MCP authorization spec) and TLS in front of it.

findings.message: MCP tool opens a file path taken directly from a tool argument
findings.guidance: Resolve the path against a fixed base directory and reject anything outside it (Path.resolve().is_relative_to(base)).

findings.message: Vector database client connects without TLS or without credentials
findings.guidance: Connect over HTTPS with an API key or token taken from the environment. Embeddings and the documents stored with them are sensitive data.

findings.message: HTML is rendered from a non-constant value
findings.guidance: Render text, not HTML. If HTML is required, sanitise it with a maintained sanitiser (DOMPurify) immediately before rendering.

findings.message: SQL statement is built from a template string or concatenation
findings.guidance: Use parameterised queries ($1, $2 with a values array) or the query builder; never interpolate values into SQL text.

findings.message: A password is hardcoded in source
findings.guidance: Do not ship credentials in client or server code. For a demo login, create the session server-side or use a restricted, rate-limited demo account whose credentials are not in the bundle.

notes: Bundled EAF rule file only; no rules are downloaded and metrics are off.
Pattern matching within a single file: no cross-file data flow.
Inline 'nosemgrep' comments in the source are honoured.
Scanner self-test passed (planted canary was detected).

checks.title: PostgreSQL / pgvector access-control rules (built-in)

findings.message: Role password is written as a literal in a SQL file
findings.guidance: Create roles without a password in migrations and set credentials through the secret store / deployment tooling. Rotate this one.

findings.message: Policy on 'documents' allows ALL for role 'public' without any row condition (USING (true))
findings.guidance: Replace the unconditional 'true' with a predicate that ties the row to the caller (owner, tenant or role). If public access is intended, restrict it to SELECT and document why.

findings.message: Write privileges (all) granted to 'anon' on table public.document_chunks
findings.guidance: Grant only the privileges each role needs; do not grant write access to anonymous or PUBLIC roles.

findings.message: SECURITY DEFINER function 'match_chunks' does not pin search_path
findings.guidance: Add 'SET search_path = <schema>, pg_temp' (or '') to every SECURITY DEFINER function, and prefer SECURITY INVOKER unless elevated rights are required.

findings.message: Vector similarity function 'match_chunks' is SECURITY DEFINER and therefore bypasses row level security on the embeddings table
findings.guidance: Embeddings can reveal the text they were computed from. Protect vector tables with the same row-level rules as the source data and filter similarity searches by tenant/user inside the query.

findings.message: Function 'purge_table' builds dynamic SQL by concatenation (EXECUTE ... || ...)
findings.guidance: Use format() with %I / %L, or EXECUTE ... USING parameters.

findings.message: Vector table 'document_chunks' has no row level security; tenant isolation depends entirely on application code
findings.guidance: Embeddings can reveal the text they were computed from. Protect vector tables with the same row-level rules as the source data and filter similarity searches by tenant/user inside the query.

findings.message: Row level security is enabled on 'audit_log' but no policy is defined in the scanned files; only privileged roles can access it
findings.guidance: If the table is used by clients, add explicit policies; if it is server-only, state that in a comment in the migration.

findings.message: Vector table 'document_chunks' has no HNSW/IVFFlat index; similarity search will scan the whole table
findings.guidance: Add an approximate-nearest-neighbour index (USING hnsw or ivfflat) matching the distance operator used in queries.

notes: Static rules over SQL files, evaluated in file-name order (migration order). The live database is not inspected.
No Supabase/PostgREST usage detected: missing row level security is reported as informational because access control may be enforced in the application.
3 table(s) in the public schema tracked, 1 with vector columns, 2 with row level security enabled.

checks.title: A written specification exists

findings.message: Not found: A written specification exists. Looked for: spec/*, specs/*, docs/spec*, docs/specs/*, docs/requirements*, requirements/*, docs/prd*, prd.md ...
findings.guidance: Without a written specification nobody can tell whether the code does what was intended, and reviewers of AI-generated code have nothing to review against. Before changing code, write or update a short spec per feature (for example specs/<feature>.md): the problem, the intended behaviour, inputs and outputs, error cases, and what is explicitly out of scope. Give the spec to the AI assistant as the task input instead of a one-line prompt, and change the spec first when requirements change.

checks.title: Specifications contain testable acceptance criteria

findings.message: Not found: Specifications contain testable acceptance criteria. Looked for: spec/*, specs/*, docs/spec*, docs/specs/*, docs/requirements*, requirements/*, docs/prd*, prd.md ...
findings.guidance: A spec that cannot be tested cannot be verified. Acceptance criteria are what turns a description into something a test or a reviewer can check. For each requirement add acceptance criteria that can be checked: numbered requirements (REQ-001 ...) or Given/When/Then scenarios. Reference the requirement id in the test that covers it.

checks.title: README explains purpose, setup, usage and testing

findings.message: README has no section about: usage / how to run
findings.guidance: A new team member, a reviewer or an auditor should be able to build, run and test the project from the README alone. Add the missing sections to README.md. Keep each to a few lines with the exact commands. When you change how the project is built, run or tested, update the README in the same change.

checks.title: Architecture or design decisions are documented

findings.message: Not found: Architecture or design decisions are documented. Looked for: docs/architecture*, architecture.md, docs/design*, design.md, docs/adr/*, adr/*, docs/decisions/*, docs/arc42* ...
findings.guidance: Structure that exists only in the code (or only in an AI chat history) is lost. Undocumented architecture is the main reason generated code drifts into inconsistency. Add docs/architecture.md with the main components, their responsibilities, data flow and external interfaces. Record significant decisions as short ADRs (docs/adr/0001-<title>.md: context, decision, consequences) at the time they are made.

checks.title: Changes are recorded (changelog or release notes)

findings.message: Not found: Changes are recorded (changelog or release notes). Looked for: changelog*, changes.md, history.md, release-notes*, releases.md, docs/changelog*, docs/release*, .changeset/*
findings.guidance: Users and reviewers need to know what changed between versions without reading every commit. Add CHANGELOG.md in 'Keep a Changelog' format and add an entry in the same change that alters behaviour. Use semantic versioning for releases.

checks.title: Contribution and review process is defined

findings.message: Not found: Contribution and review process is defined. Looked for: contributing*, docs/contributing*, .github/pull_request_template*, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/*, codeowners, .github/codeowners, docs/codeowners, .gitlab/merge_request_templates/* ...
findings.guidance: Generated code needs the same review as hand-written code. A defined process (who reviews, what must be true before merge) is what makes that enforceable. Add CONTRIBUTING.md (branching, commit and review rules, definition of done), a pull request template with a checklist (spec updated, tests added, EAF run attached) and a CODEOWNERS file.

checks.title: Security policy or threat model is documented

findings.message: Not found: Security policy or threat model is documented. Looked for: security.md, .github/security.md, docs/security*, docs/threat*, threat-model*, docs/tara*
findings.guidance: IT security reviewers ask first how vulnerabilities are reported and which threats were considered. Without a document the answer is 'none'. Add SECURITY.md (how to report a vulnerability, supported versions) and, for anything networked, a short threat model: assets, entry points, trust boundaries, and the mitigations you rely on.

checks.title: Documentation is updated together with the code
notes: Last documentation commit is 0 day(s) older than the last code commit.

checks.title: The REST API has a machine-readable contract (OpenAPI)
notes: Evidence: openapi.json

checks.title: Database schema changes are versioned migrations
notes: Evidence: db/migrations/001_init.sql, db/migrations/002_search.sql

checks.title: MCP servers and their tools are documented
notes: Evidence: README.md

checks.title: AI coding assistants have project instructions

findings.message: Not found: AI coding assistants have project instructions. Looked for: agents.md, claude.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*, .cursor/rules/*, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, .clinerules ...
findings.guidance: Without project rules an assistant falls back to generic patterns. That is what produces inconsistent structure, duplicated helpers and unreviewed dependencies. Add AGENTS.md (or .github/copilot-instructions.md) stating: where the spec lives and that it must be read first, architecture rules, coding conventions, how to run tests and EAF, what the assistant must not do (add dependencies, change schemas, weaken checks) without asking.

limitations: Level 1 inspects source text only: nothing is built, executed or tested.
A PASS reflects the configured tools and thresholds only; absence of findings is not absence of defects.
Engineering-practice checks establish that a document exists and has minimal substance. They do not judge whether it is correct, complete or followed.
Standards coverage is partial by construction: a mapped category means some checks look for instances of that weakness class, not that the category is satisfied.
